content:
Earlier this year in July, Apple added basic search functionality to its TestFlight app. While you might think such a simple update would be widely welcomed, the same version of TestFlight introduced a rather frustrating bug for many users.

Personally, I didn't notice being affected by the bug. As a result, I considered the TestFlight update a simple but meaningful improvement at the time.

Sometimes, a small change can have a big impact. This is especially true for users with a large number of pre-loaded apps, following Apple's latest TestFlight update. Apple has just updated TestFlight for iPhone, iPad, Mac, and other platforms. The new version 4.3 adds a 'search bar to quickly find apps' feature.

Looking back, I did notice a few odd things, which I flagged at the end of the article (though my assessment at the time was exactly the opposite):

I think the reason I missed that this was actually the bug is because I keep TestFlight betas from apps I've participated in over the years, in order to 'merge' my previously separate iCloud and App Store Apple accounts last year. While it's a bit inconvenient, it's been worth it for me.

In any case, the TestFlight bug wasn't overlooked, and John Vorhees of MacStories also mentioned it:

So you can imagine my excitement when I read Zac Hall of 9to5Mac writing about the new search bar in TestFlight. I thought, 'Finally!' I immediately dropped what I was doing and updated the app. […] Unfortunately, there's a big 'but' behind this update. Previously, TestFlight betas were listed in reverse chronological order, which I quite liked. […] Now, expired betas are mixed in with active TestFlight betas, sorted alphabetically, and the number of expired betas appears to have expanded to include every beta I've ever participated in. I did a rough count, and for me it's nearly 800 app listings. As you can see, very few of the active betas remain. The search function helps with finding things, but it's no longer possible to scroll through them.

Then in August, John Gruber wrote an article on Daring Fireball discussing the TestFlight update and the bug:

Last night, more than a month after the bug appeared (and was pointed out by Vorhees), Apple finally updated TestFlight for the first time. While the update notes only mention bug fixes, the update does address the issue in question.

TestFlight version 4.3.1 is the fix provided for users experiencing this regression issue.
